ios.desc:
Wyrm Math turns algebra into something you do with your hands.

Instead of typing commands or watching a video, you solve equations by direct touch — drag a
term across the equals sign and it flips sign, pull a factor apart, split a fraction. The
equation responds to your gestures in real time.

The difference: Wyrm only ever lets you make legal moves. Every change goes through a real
math engine, so an illegal step simply isn't possible. You can't break the math — which means
you're free to experiment, and what you learn is the actual structure of algebra, not a set of
memorized tricks.

WHAT YOU CAN DO
- Solve by dragging — move terms, factor, distribute, cancel, and split fractions with your fingers
- Play the campaign — a star-rated game mode that dares you to solve in as few moves as possible
- See every step — a running derivation you can scroll back through and learn from
- Track the fine print — when a move depends on a condition (like a denominator ≠ 0), Wyrm shows
  it as an assumption you can tap to trace
- Get unstuck — "Guide me" coaches you toward the next legal move without doing it for you
- Explore freely — try a "what-if," check your solution, or back up and take a different path

GAME MODE — BEAT PAR
Game mode is an algebra game with a score. Every equation has a par: the fewest moves it takes
to solve. You get a fresh problem, your moves are counted, and the solve is rated against par —
three stars if you match it. Seven stages climb from one-step equations through variables on
both sides, distribution, fractions, and powers to quadratics, each with its own colors and
sound. Earn enough stars to advance; beat par and you bank an undo token to spend on a harder
problem later. There's no coaching and no free undo here — you already know your moves are
legal. The only challenge is finding the shortest path. Unlike most math games, the notation is
real and so is the algebra.

FROM FIRST EQUATIONS TO REAL ALGEBRA
Start with one-step equations like x + 2 = 5 and work all the way up to multi-step linear
equations and the quadratic formula. Wyrm grows with you.

BUILT FOR LEARNING BY DOING
Whether you're a student trying to actually understand algebra, a parent helping with homework,
or anyone who wants to rebuild their math intuition, Wyrm replaces "follow these steps" with
"try it and see why it works."

No accounts. No ads. No data collection. Just you and the math.

android.desc:
Wyrm Math turns algebra into something you solve with your hands. Drag a term across the equals sign, pull out a shared factor, cancel, distribute — every move is a real algebraic step, and the equation transforms as you go.

The twist: you literally can't make an illegal move. The app only ever offers transformations that are mathematically valid, so you can experiment freely and trust that anything you derive is actually true. No guessing, no "wrong answer" buzzers — just algebra you can feel.

WHAT YOU CAN SOLVE
• Linear equations — one-step, two-step, and variables on both sides
• Distribution and combining like terms
• Fractions and clearing denominators
• Powers and roots
• Quadratics — including the quadratic formula, step by step
• Systems of equations
• Inequalities

LEARN, DON'T JUST ANSWER
• Guide me — gentle, tap-by-tap hints that show your next move without doing it for you
• Every solution is a full, replayable set of steps
• Check your answer and explore "what if" instantly
• Tap Random problem in any topic for endless, guaranteed-solvable practice

NEW: GAME MODE
A star-rated campaign across 7 stages — solve each equation in as few moves as possible and beat par to earn three stars. A relaxed algebra game you can't lose, but can always get better at.

BUILT FOR REAL LEARNING
Great for students working through homework, adults refreshing pre-algebra and algebra, homeschoolers, and anyone who wants the concepts to finally click through hands-on practice.

HONEST AND PRIVATE
• One-time purchase — no subscription, ever
• No ads, no account, no analytics
• Works fully offline

Real notation. Real equations. Learn algebra by moving it.

The idea at its core: only legal moves are possible. Equations change only through sound algebraic rules, so you can never make an invalid step. Explore, experiment, and trust that every move is real algebra. And everything is exact — true fractions and exact roots, never rounded-off decimals.

Stuck? Two kinds of help:
• Guide me — an interactive coach. A finger shows you the next move, then waits for you to do it. It adapts to wherever you are, so you learn by doing, not by watching.
• Solution Search — let the app find a complete solution and play it through, step by step (beta).

What Wyrm solves:
• Linear equations — one side or both, with parentheses and fractions
• Inequalities, including the sign-flip when you divide by a negative
• Powers and quotients of powers

quotes.text:
There is a mobile game called DragonBox. It sort of tricks you into learning algebra by starting with very abstract manipulations of a puzzle that must follow rules... gradually the game teaches you more and more rules and also strips out the more abstract elements until on the last levels you are finally solving real equations. I loved it, it taught my kids algebra.... and it was just fun.

Over the years I often thought that there should be a calculator for Algebra that works this way... something where you can drag terms around and cancel & distribute with gestures, but most importantly enter your own problems.  It should also do more kinds of problems than DragonBox allowed. So I finally decided to build it.

https://dicroce.github.io/wyrm/home.html

Here's a video showing it: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_STbS4zvIlU. If you'd rather just play with it: there's a limited in-browser demo (real engine, a few example equations, no download) on the landing page — https://dicroce.github.io/wyrm/home.html.

The app can be found on iOS (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/wyrm-math/id6782342042) and as of this week on Google Play (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.dicroce.wyrm).

I also decided to open source the underlying math engine so others could build on it: https://github.com/dicroce/wyrm_math. My goal for the engine btw is to build it all the way up to Calculus.
